messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Admission Date: March 2017

Discharge Date: August 2018
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Initial Presentation:

The patient presented with complaints of abdominal pain for 2 months and aggravated for 1 week, leading to the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma.

Management:

The patient was assessed by our Multi-Disciplinary Treatment (MDT) team, who recommended initiating palliative chemotherapy treatment along with apatinib. The patient tolerated the treatment well with only Grade 2 neutropenia and Grade 1 vomiting observed during treatment. Post-treatment CT scans revealed partial response with further tumor shrinkage during treatment.

Surgical Intervention:

The patient underwent total gastrectomy, D2 lymph node dissection, and Roux-en-Y anastomosis in August 2017 after being evaluated for acceptable radical surgery. The postoperative pathology report indicates no residual cancer tissue found in the resected tissue sample.

Post-Surgery Management:

After the surgical procedure, the patient recovered well and underwent maintenance treatment with apatinib in the same dose as before. No adverse events were noted in the postoperative period. However, in August 2018, the patient's ascites worsened, and adenocarcinoma cells were found by ascites biopsy, indicating disease progression.

Outcome:

The patient passed away in September 2018. The progression-free survival (PFS) period was 12 months, and the overall survival (OS) period was 17 months.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is gastric adenocarcinoma, a malignant neoplasm of the stomach. It was treated with chemotherapy plus apatinib and then total gastrectomy. It belongs to chapter C (neoplasms), and the stomach category is C16. Peritoneal spread with ascites is secondary disease, so it does not change the principal diagnosis.

CODE: C16
